A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FedMIA and provide readable main text, Tables 1–3, Figures 1–6, and Appendices A–C. The material supports a complete comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original membership-inference experiments on classification and diffusion models, including attack comparisons, defense evaluations, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix B, including Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–6.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same measurements, Gaussian estimation from non-target updates, three-sigma filtering, and averaging of round-wise membership scores. Section 3.3 expands and qualifies the filtering explanation without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-100, DermNet, and Tiny-ImageNet for the same classification and image-generation tasks. The evaluated federated structures, defenses, and IID/non-IID scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Blackbox-Loss, Grad-Cosine, Grad-Norm, Loss-Series, Avg-Cosine, and Grad-Diff. The corresponding comparator subsets in the defense and sensitivity experiments are unchanged. Newly cited secure-aggregation methods are discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4.1, Appendix A, and Table 3 retain the same splits, preprocessing, model configurations, training settings, parameter sweeps, and evaluation metrics. Table 1's ResNet-to-ResNet18 label correction matches the architecture already specified in v2.

E4.justification: The generated-image case study, defense trade-offs, non-IID tests, and analyses of communication rounds, client counts, sample counts, and local epochs remain unchanged in Figures 3–6 and Appendix B. No filtering ablation or secure-aggregation experiment is added.

E5.justification: Table 1 and Section 4.2 replace '+' with '±' between the same estimates and accompanying quantities, clarifying uncertainty notation. Neither version specifies what those quantities represent or supplies run counts or seeds; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the attribution of the 66.98% AlexNet-CIFAR100 TPR from FedMIA-Loss to FedMIA-II and removes the incorrect Grad-Cosine attribution for 54.66%, which Table 1 assigns to Avg-Cosine. Table values and figure results are unchanged. However, v3 adds percent signs to prose AUC values 0.62 and 0.52, creating inconsistencies with Table 1.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, disjoint-data and Gaussian assumptions, Theorem 1, hypervolume definition, and Appendix C proof are retained. Closing-parenthesis and bracket corrections are typographical; the added filtering qualification is informal discussion.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about the non-target-update test, three-step attack, classification and generation performance, compatibility with existing measurements, and robustness to the tested defenses. The added defense discussion does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 qualifies the claim that filtering excludes target-trained updates with 'high probability.' Section 5 newly argues that secure aggregation using MPC or homomorphic encryption blocks FedMIA, discusses its computational and communication costs, and identifies access to non-target updates as a defense-design concern.

D1.justification: Appendix A and Table 3 retain the same data-construction instructions, defense parameters, optimizers, learning rates, training budgets, and GPU information. The code-access link is unchanged, and no additional implementation or reproducibility information is supplied.

R1.justification: v3 adds four secure-aggregation references: SafeLearn, SafeFL, Wibawa et al.'s encrypted CNN training work, and BatchCrypt. These support the new defense discussion. The previous 47 references remain; their extensive renumbering reflects bibliography reordering.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar and notation corrections, updates an author affiliation, expands the filtering explanation, and renames Section 5 'Discussion and Conclusion.' It also removes an empty Appendix A.1 heading and renumbers the retained subsections. The overall narrative structure remains stable.

P2.justification: Table 1 changes column spacing, vertical rules, and uncertainty notation. Figure 3 moves from the upper right to the lower left of page 6, and surrounding text and references reflow. All six figures retain their contents, and no figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 makes a limited improvement by explicitly discussing the secure-aggregation boundary, qualifying the filtering claim, correcting a result attribution, and clarifying uncertainty notation. These gains are tempered by newly inconsistent AUC percent signs in Section 4.2 and the continued absence of explanations for the reported uncertainty. The method, experimental evidence, and proofs remain unchanged.
